claim_summary: For m=2k, uniform site colorings h:[n]->[m] plus color signs xi produce a nonnegative unbiased rainbow-Pfaffian estimator Z/p, where p=m!/m^m. A weighted Pfaffian norm q_k(W A* W A), extracted by a color-subset Mobius difference, computes Z exactly in 4^k coefficient calls. Its total exact relative-estimation cost is (16 e^2)^k poly(n,L,eta^-1,log(1/delta)), so it is universal but asymptotically worse than c03_l10's C_k poly(n,L,...) route for low-k sectors.

finite_check.full_color_average: equals p*c in all four cases
finite_check.naive_counterexample: 2x2 swap F, k=1: c=2; rainbow color difference with all signs + is 0; averaging independent color signs returns 2
finite_check.coloring_sampling_boundary: 4x4 cross identity at k=2 has one nonzero pair, c=1, and exactly 24/256 rainbow colorings; p=3/32 and relative variance of c_h/p is 29/3, showing the Omega(1/p) coloring cost for this estimator only
